title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing p.33): M is a motive over R, with K = C. Its Betti realization is V = H^*(X(C),Q). The real Frobenius f = F_inf is an involution of V, and sigma denotes complex conjugation on the coefficients of V_C = V (x)_Q C. The de Rham realization DR(M) is a real vector space with comparison DR(M) (x)_R C = V_C. The real structure DR(M) inside V_C is the fixed locus of the twisted conjugation z |-> f(z-bar), i.e. f sigma z = z. Writing z = x+iy with x,y in V_R, this gives DR(M) = V_R^+ (+) i V_R^-, where V^+- are the +-1 eigenspaces of f.

Grothendieck observes that DR(M) therefore carries a natural Q-structure W = V^+ (+) i V^-. He calls it the 'twisted Betti' subspace ('sous-espace de Betti tordu'). W is stable under f. He asks whether W is compatible with tensor products and answers yes. Indeed (iV^-)(x)(iV'^-) = -(V^- (x) V'^-) lies in (V (x) V')^+, so W(M (x) M') = W(M) (x) W(M') inside (V (x) V')_C. Hence M |-> W(M) is a second Q-valued exact tensor fibre functor on the Tannakian category of motives over R.

The obvious linear isomorphism V -> W is the identity on V^+ and multiplication by i on V^-. It is natural but not tensor-compatible: on V^- (x) V'^- it is off by a sign -1. Grothendieck concludes that 'BETTI' (twisted) and Betti are presumably not isomorphic as tensor functors. Instead one is obtained from the other by twisting with the cocycle defined by f.

In modern terms, W is the Galois descent of V_{Q(i)} along Q(i)/Q using the semilinear action z |-> f(z-bar). Since f lies in G(Q) and f^2 = 1, conj |-> f is a 1-cocycle of Gal(Q(i)/Q) in G(Q(i)). Its class is the image of the quadratic torsor Spec Q(i) (the class of -1 in H^1(Q,Z/2) = Q*/Q*^2) under the map H^1(Q,Z/2) -> H^1(Q,G) induced by f: Z/2 -> G_M. The torsor Isom^(x)(omega_B, omega_W) is the corresponding G-torsor over Q, split by Q(i).

The margin records the inclusions V superset V cap W = V^f = W^f subset W, and identifies H^*(X(R),Q) with V cap W = V^f.
errors: The marginal identification H^*(X(R),Q) = V cap W = V^f is false in general. V cap W is just V^+ = H^*(X(C),Q)^{F_inf}, which is not the cohomology of the real locus: for example X(R) can be empty while V^+ contains at least H^0. One also has V cap W = V^+ and W^f = V^+, so V^f = W^f is correct, but the link to X(R) is not.

The statement 'il est isomorphe au premier' is retracted on the same page (the isomorphism is not tensor-compatible). The final conclusion, 'not isomorphic but a twist by the f-cocycle', is the correct one. In some cases the torsor is trivial: for the Tate motive Q(1), G = G_m and f = -1 = g/g-bar with g = i. For the Artin motive Spec C over R, G = Z/2 and the torsor is Spec Q(i), which is non-trivial.

ideas.what: Real de Rham structure of a motive over R as fixed points of F_inf composed with complex conjugation: DR_R = V_R^+ (+) i V_R^-
ideas.modern_name: Real structure on de Rham via F_inf (x) c; Hodge structures over R
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales' (1979)

ideas.what: Natural Q-structure W = V^+ (+) iV^- on the real de Rham space ('Betti tordu'), forming a second tensor fibre functor
ideas.modern_name: Twisted Betti fibre functor; Galois descent of omega_B (x) Q(i) via F_inf (x) conj
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; implicit in period computations (Deligne 1979, the c^+/c^- periods)

ideas.what: The two Q-fibre functors differ by twisting by the torsor given by the cocycle conj |-> F_inf in H^1(Gal(Q(i)/Q), G_M)
ideas.modern_name: Twisting of fibre functors by torsors in Tannakian categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972) for the general theory; Deligne-Milne (1982)

missed.claim: Grothendieck identifies a canonical Q-structure on the real de Rham realization of a motive over R. He also identifies the class of the corresponding motivic Galois torsor: the image of [Q(i)] under the map H^1(Q,Z/2) -> H^1(Q,G_M) given by F_inf. He does not pursue when this class vanishes, or its relation to the 2-pi-i factors in Deligne's periods c^+-.
missed.quote: Il semble que BETTI et Betti ne sont pas isomorphes, l'un est déduit de l'autre en tordant par le cocycle défini par f|R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a clean Tannakian way to phrase the sign and power-of-i ambiguities in real periods (Deligne's c^+ versus c^- periods). It is a minor but explicit framing; similar remarks are folklore in the periods literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct and early (c.1970) Tannakian formulation of the twisted Betti Q-structure on real de Rham cohomology. It includes the observation that this structure is a torsor-twist of Betti by the real Frobenius cocycle. That predates Deligne 1979, but the underlying facts are standard and the idea is close to folklore.
transcription_corrections: 'mérite le nom de sous-espace de Betti tordu': 'tordu' is written above a struck 'Betti', so the intended phrase is 'Betti tordu'.
Margin line 2 reads 'H^*(X(R),Q) = V cap W = V^f = W^f' with W in the right column.
'cet isom n'est pas compatible avec les produits tensoriels' ('pas' is underlined).
Last lines: 'Il semble que BETTI et Betti ne sont pas [isomorphes] (on ne trouve pas [d']isom.), l'un est déduit (Betti tordu) de l'autre en tordant par le cocycle défini par f_R'.
